subject: Full lists in day fields: canonical text, descriptions and lint follow the either rule
brief:
Several cronlite helpers treat a day field that lists every value as if it were a star. With the classic either-day-or-weekday rule that is wrong: such a list is still a restriction, so when the other day field is a list too, the full list always matches and the expression runs every day. Make canonical text, equivalence, descriptions and warnings follow what the expression really does. Matching itself already follows the rule and must not change.

1. Add `CronExpr.day_restrictions()`, returning a pair of booleans: whether the day of month really restricts the days the expression runs on, and whether the weekday does. When both day fields are lists (neither is written as a star) and either list covers every value of its field, neither restricts; when both are lists and neither is full, both restrict. When at least one of them is a star, a field restricts exactly when it is a list that leaves out some value.
2. `canonical` writes each day field as a star when it does not restrict and as its sorted list when it does; minute, hour and month keep today's rule (a full list is written as a star), and aliases still apply to the result. As a consequence `equivalent` tells apart a list of every weekday next to a day number (every day) from a star next to that day number (one day a month).
3. `describe` leaves out the date part of a day field that does not restrict, so an expression that runs every day reads like one with two stars; expressions where both day fields restrict keep the either-rule wording.
4. `lint` judges the day fields the same way: `day-and-weekday` only when both restrict; the month-length warnings only when the day of month restricts and the weekday does not; `every-minute` when minute, hour and month are full and neither day field restricts. Add a new warning code `every-day` for an expression whose two day fields are both lists but one of them lists every value, so it runs every day; it takes the place where `day-and-weekday` would stand in the list of codes, before the others. A full list next to a star is just a long way of writing a star: it gets neither `every-day` nor any other day warning.
5. `duplicates` (and so `lint_all`) groups schedules by their canonical text, so differently written expressions that fire at the same minutes are duplicates and ones that only look alike are not.

All behavior that the existing tests check must keep working.
